description: Declares which vault items are portable to user-level Claude Code config (~/.claude/) and which are vault-specific. Read by scripts/sync-to-profile.sh.

agents.rationale: omc-adapted agents are pure software engineering — no vault dependencies. Safe to install at user level so they work in every project.

commands.rationale: Portable versions live in scripts/portable/commands/ so the vault keeps its richer vault-aware versions at .claude/commands/. Vault versions shadow user-level versions when working inside the vault.

playbooks.rationale: Playbooks are not a standard Claude Code folder, but creating ~/.claude/playbooks/ is harmless and makes them discoverable. Referenced by the user-level CLAUDE.md snippet.

claude_md_section.rationale: A single managed section is appended or replaced in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Everything between the start and end markers is owned by the sync script; the rest of the user's CLAUDE.md is untouched.

agents.rationale: Vault-native agents depend on brain/, work/, org/, perf/, bases/. They would fail in non-vault projects.

commands.rationale: Most commands assume vault folders, Obsidian wikilinks, or vault-specific workflows.

hooks.rationale: All hooks (session-start, classify-message, validate-write, pre-compact, stop-checklist) are vault-aware and would fail or produce wrong output in non-vault projects. They stay project-level.

skills.rationale: Obsidian-specific skills (obsidian-markdown, obsidian-cli, obsidian-bases, json-canvas) only make sense inside an Obsidian vault. defuddle and qmd are general but have their own install flows.

brain_topic_notes.rationale: All brain/ topic notes depend on the vault structure and conventions. They stay in the vault as the single source of truth — the user-level CLAUDE.md snippet references them as concepts but doesn't copy them.

backup_policy.description: Before overwriting any existing user-level file, sync-to-profile.sh copies it to a timestamped backup so the previous state is recoverable.

provenance.description: After a successful sync, a provenance file is written recording which version of the vault installed these items, when, and from where. Future syncs read this to know what to update vs leave alone.
